Yes — I found several small, locally based studios/agencies in Etobicoke that look relevant for an independent shop. I’d focus on teams that can handle creative + practical local marketing rather than a big corporate agency.

A few worth checking out

Julie Studios Creative Agency — Etobicoke-based and particularly interesting if you need branding, social media, photography and video together. Their work appears geared toward small/mid-sized businesses and product/food/lifestyle imagery.

CCS Studio Inc. — A boutique creative/digital studio on The Queensway. Its listed strengths include photo/video, social content, web presence and digital marketing, which could suit a neighbourhood retail business.

X Square — On Manitoba St. and offers branding, website work, social content, photography/video and local advertising. Their portfolio specifically includes a barbershop/local-business project.

The Epiq Marketing Agency — In Long Branch and describes itself as working with small and medium-sized businesses, with a creative emphasis including social content and reels.

WordzOut — On The West Mall. More social-media focused, with content creation, newsletters, SMS, local event coverage and video. They also publish starting prices for some social packages, which is useful when you're a small shop.

mrge Marketing — A boutique agency on Lake Shore Blvd W. It leans more toward marketing strategy, content, SEO, campaigns and ongoing support than purely visual creative work.

There's also Build With Social, a multidisciplinary studio right on Park Lawn Rd. that explicitly says it works with local brands. 
Build With Social

If it's a neighbourhood shop

I'd tell prospective studios something like: “We're a small local shop and need someone who can make us look good online without turning this into a huge agency engagement.” Then ask for:

A small monthly package — e.g. social content + a few photos/reels + Google Business Profile.

Examples from retail/food/local businesses, not just corporate clients.

Whether they can do on-site shoots at your shop.

Their minimum monthly commitment and total monthly cost.

Whether you'll work directly with the creative person or through an account manager.

If you tell me what kind of shop it is (bakery, clothing, salon, specialty food, gift shop, etc.) and roughly what you'd like to spend per month, I can narrow this to 3–4 particularly relevant options and compare what each offers.
